naming_clarity.reason: Deliberately plain wording (remaining charge, remaining capacity, predicted range) instead of state-of-charge/state-of-health jargon; a non-implementer stakeholder could confirm every term unaided.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: No class, function, module, table, internal endpoint or technology choice appears; dashboard and fleet report are user-facing surfaces rather than implementation constructs.

parent_fit.reason: user_story is the root stage of this project V and the need carries no outgoing parent link, so per the pack scoring guide this axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: Two independently deliverable capabilities get equal billing in title and body: a dashboard remaining-charge figure serving driver/range trust, and a fleet-report remaining-capacity (degradation) figure serving pack-replacement planning. Each has its own user, its own observation surface and its own goal clause, and either could ship without the other.
single_user_capability.suggestion: Split into two stories: (1) report a remaining charge the vehicle user can trust, evidenced by the dashboard level staying within a stated tolerance of the energy actually delivered and not jumping across an off/on cycle; (2) report how much of the original capacity the pack has lost, evidenced by a fleet-report figure that only decreases and a workshop full discharge/recharge cross-check. Any shared measurement basis between the two belongs in the downstream requirements, not fused into one story.

user_observable.reason: Every claim is checkable from outside the pack: dashboard charge level against the energy the vehicle actually delivers, stability across a power cycle, a monotonically decreasing capacity figure in the fleet report, and a workshop full-cycle confirmation against energy that physically went in and out.

summary: Clearly written and fully observable, but it fuses two independently deliverable reports (remaining charge for range trust, remaining capacity for replacement planning) into one story. 8/10.
